reader_summary.headline: A radical change of direction in attitude, goals.
reader_summary.overview: A radical change of direction in attitude, goals. In my 53 years in the investment world, I've seen a number of economic cycles, pendulum swings, manias and panics, bubbles and crashes. But I remember only two real sea changes.

key_points.text: I think we may be in the midst of a third one today.

key_points.evidence_quote: As I've recounted many times in my memos, when I joined the investment management industry in 1969, many banks, like the one I worked for at the time, focused their equity portfolios on the so-called Nifty-50.

key_points.text: The Nifty-50 comprised the stocks of companies that were considered the best and fastest growing.
key_points.evidence_quote: The Nifty-50 comprised the stocks of companies that were considered the best and fastest growing, so good that nothing bad could ever happen to them.

key_points.text: For these stocks, everyone was sure there was no price too high.

thesis: The speaker identifies two historical sea changes in investing: the shift in the mid-1970s toward a risk-return mindset that enabled high-yield bonds and private equity, and the subsequent four-decade decline in interest rates driven by Paul Volker's control of inflation. He argues that this combination of factors, particularly the massive drop in interest rates, created an incredible tailwind that fueled economic growth, corporate profitability, and a compound annual stock market return of 10.3% per year.
